name: The builders of Babel
charge: Building a city and a tower under Nimrod, to make themselves a name and be one people, lest they be scattered abroad
summary: Cush was the father of Nimrod, the mighty hunter before the Lord, and the beginning of his kingdom was Babel in the land of Shinar, built on the same ground where Cain had built his city. One people with one language, they raised a tower to make themselves a name and not be scattered, the flood still in their memory, and they raised it in rivalry rather than in reverence. The Most High confounded their speech, scattered them, and separated the nations, sending every family to its own place. The gathering of all nations as one is the spirit of the man of sin.
offenseFull: Cush fathered Nimrod, who began to be a mighty one in the earth, a mighty hunter before the Lord; the beginning of his kingdom was Babel, and Erech, and Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar, and out of that land Asshur went forth and builded Nineveh (Genesis 10:8-11). Shinar is the country now called Iraq. Mighty hunter is not a compliment; it says he hunted men and was an evil ruler. The Sumerians called Erech by the name Unug, and the older scholars identified that with the city Cain built and called after his son, so Nimrod raised the beginning of his kingdom on the ruins of Cain’s, and came into the same wisdom that was there. History records him as the first king of that place, the first mortal deified at his death and called the father of the gods; from him, from his queen and from her child came the first pagan trinity, whose worship spread through every nation under other names, and the sun worship behind Sunday sacredness, Christmas and Easter. That country was so far gone that the Most High afterward called one man, Abram, to get out of it.

The whole earth was of one language and of one speech, and as they journeyed from the east they found a plain in the land of Shinar and dwelt there (Genesis 11:1-2). They built the tower so that they would not be scattered abroad upon the face of the whole earth, and to make themselves a name (Genesis 11:3-4). The flood was still in their memory, and the tower was not raised to honour the One who sent it; it was raised against him. It stood against the word given to Noah’s sons, to replenish the earth (Genesis 9:1). And it was no ordinary work of brick and slime, because the Most High himself said the people were one, and that now nothing would be restrained from them which they had imagined to do (Genesis 11:6). Wisdom calls it the wicked conspiracy of the nations (Wisdom of Solomon 10:5). The people being one was never going to produce righteousness. Unity is agreement upon the laws of God; unity out of self will is what the psalm describes, the kings of the earth setting themselves and the rulers taking counsel together against the Lord and against his anointed, and though hand join in hand, they shall not go unpunished (Psalms 2:1-4; Proverbs 16:5).
judgmentFull: The Lord came down, confounded their language so that they could not understand one another’s speech, and scattered them abroad from thence upon the face of all the earth, and they left off to build the city; the name of it is Babel, which is confusion (Genesis 11:7-9). The scattering was not only a penalty. It was an order restored. The Most High divided to the nations their inheritance and separated the sons of Adam, and set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel, for the Lord’s portion is his people and Jacob is the lot of his inheritance (Deuteronomy 32:7-9). Every family was sent back where it belonged, Ham to his place, Shem to his, Japheth to his, every one after his tongue, after his family, and in his nation (Genesis 10:5, 20, 31-32). In the days of Peleg the earth was divided (Genesis 10:25).

There has never been a doctrine in the scriptures of all the nations holding hands as one. The man of sin opposes the separation: he exalts himself above all that is called God, gathers the nations to himself, sits as God and shows himself that he is God, which is the same thing Nimrod did in the land of Shinar (2 Thessalonians 2:3-4). And the judgment runs like a ring. Babylon ruled at the beginning, on that ground, and Babylon rules at the end; the city was left unfinished, and every empire since has tried to finish it.

text.text: And Cush begat Nimrod: he began to be a mighty one in the earth.
He was a mighty hunter before the Lord: wherefore it is said, Even as Nimrod the mighty hunter before the Lord.
And the beginning of his kingdom was Babel, and Erech, and Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.
Out of that land went forth Asshur, and builded Nineveh, and the city Rehoboth, and Calah,
And the whole earth was of one language, and of one speech.
And it came to pass, as they journeyed from the east, that they found a plain in the land of Shinar; and they dwelt there.
And they said one to another, Go to, let us make brick, and burn them throughly. And they had brick for stone, and slime had they for morter.
And they said, Go to, let us build us a city and a tower, whose top may reach unto heaven; and let us make us a name, lest we be scattered abroad upon the face of the whole earth.
And God blessed Noah and his sons, and said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth.
And the Lord came down to see the city and the tower, which the children of men builded.
And the Lord said, Behold, the people is one, and they have all one language; and this they begin to do: and now nothing will be restrained from them, which they have imagined to do.
Go to, let us go down, and there confound their language, that they may not understand one another’s speech.
So the Lord scattered them abroad from thence upon the face of all the earth: and they left off to build the city.
Therefore is the name of it called Babel; because the Lord did there confound the language of all the earth: and from thence did the Lord scatter them abroad upon the face of all the earth.
Moreover, the nations in their wicked conspiracy being confounded, she found out the righteous, and preserved him blameless unto God, and kept him strong against his tender compassion toward his son.
Why do the heathen rage, and the people imagine a vain thing?
The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together, against the Lord, and against his anointed, saying,
Let us break their bands asunder, and cast away their cords from us.
He that sitteth in the heavens shall laugh: the Lord shall have them in derision.
Every one that is proud in heart is an abomination to the Lord: though hand join in hand, he shall not be unpunished.
Remember the days of old, consider the years of many generations: ask thy father, and he will shew thee; thy elders, and they will tell thee.
When the most High divided to the nations their inheritance, when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel.
For the Lord’s portion is his people; Jacob is the lot of his inheritance.
By these were the isles of the Gentiles divided in their lands; every one after his tongue, after their families, in their nations.
These are the sons of Ham, after their families, after their tongues, in their countries, and in their nations.
And unto Eber were born two sons: the name of one was Peleg; for in his days was the earth divided; and his brother’s name was Joktan.
These are the sons of Shem, after their families, after their tongues, in their lands, after their nations.
These are the families of the sons of Noah, after their generations, in their nations: and by these were the nations divided in the earth after the flood.
Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition;
Who opposeth and exalteth himself above all that is called God, or that is worshipped; so that he as God sitteth in the temple of God, shewing himself that he is God.
